newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, Czech Republic form plane-making venture.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, Czech Republic form plane-making venture.

text.p: Taiwan and the Czech Republic signed a plane-making deal on Saturday, with Taipei saying the deal paved the way for new cooperation between the diplomatically isolated island and eastern Europe.

The agreement to jointly manufacture the AE-270, a small commercial passenger aircraft, was signed by Taiwan's state-run Aerospace Industrial Development Corp and Aero Vodochody of the Czech Republic, state television showed.

"We will begin by making small aeroplanes. After we accomplish making small planes, we can move on to make larger ones," Economics Minister Wang Chih-kang, whose ministry oversees the state firm's operations, told a signing ceremony.

"This is the first such cooperation accord we have signed with eastern Europe," Wang said. "It sets a good foundation for development of our aerospace industry as well as future cooperations with other eastern European nations."
Taiwan and the Czech Republic planned to make some 850 AE-270 10-seat airplanes, state television said.
The venture's value was not disclosed, but local media have reported both sides would jointly invest more than US$60 million in the deal, with each holding 50 percent.

Aerospace Industrial Development would assemble the turboprop planes in Taiwan for sales in the Asia-Pacific region, while Aero Vodochody would assemble them in the Czech Republic for sales in eastern Europe.
The ministry's Committee for Aviation and Space Industry Development has said it was considering deals to jointly make passenger aircraft with Czech firms Aero Vodochody and LET G.S.
The Taiwan company declined to mention whether it was still talking with LET.
Aerospace Industrial Development, long a non-commercial military plane manufacturing centre, was converted into a state-run company in July 1996.
